In the given figure, PQRS is a square of side 2 cm and PLMN is a rectangle. The corner L of the rectangle is on the side QR. Side MN of the rectangle passes through the corner S of the square.

What is the area (in cm²) of the rectangle PLMN?

Note: The figure shown is representative.
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 220 200" width="100%" style="max-width:420px;height:auto" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="50" y="50" width="100" height="100" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><polygon points="50,50 95,150 165,110 120,10" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="34" y="48" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">P</text><text x="154" y="48" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">S</text><text x="34" y="162" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">Q</text><text x="154" y="162" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">R</text><text x="88" y="172" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">L</text><text x="170" y="115" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">M</text><text x="118" y="8" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">N</text></svg>
explanation: Placing the square with Q=(0,0), R=(2,0), S=(2,2), P=(0,2) and L=(l,0) on QR, the right angle at L and the requirement that MN (parallel to PL) passes through S forces the similar right triangles PQL and LRS-extended to compensate exactly, so the rectangle's area always equals the square's area, 2×2 = 4 cm², independent of where L sits on QR.

The diagram below shows a river system consisting of 7 segments, marked P, Q, R, S, T, U, and V. It splits the land into 5 zones, marked Z1, Z2, Z3, Z4, and Z5. We need to connect these zones using the least number of bridges. Out of the following options, which one is correct?

Note: The figure shown is representative.
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 400 260" width="100%" style="max-width:420px;height:auto" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="10" y="10" width="380" height="240" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1"/><g stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="3" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M20,150 L140,130"/><path d="M140,130 L170,20"/><path d="M140,130 L230,130"/><path d="M230,130 L190,240"/><path d="M230,130 L300,130"/><path d="M300,130 L330,240"/><path d="M300,130 L350,30"/></g><g font-size="13" fill="currentColor"><text x="55" y="145">P</text><text x="148" y="65">R</text><text x="178" y="122">Q</text><text x="198" y="185">S</text><text x="262" y="122">T</text><text x="318" y="185">U</text><text x="325" y="65">V</text><text x="55" y="90">Z2</text><text x="55" y="205">Z1</text><text x="240" y="75">Z3</text><text x="355" y="140">Z4</text><text x="245" y="205">Z5</text></g></svg>
options: Bridges on P, Q, and T
Bridges on P, Q, S, and T
Bridges on Q, R, T, and V
Bridges on P, Q, S, U, and V
explanation: The river's segments form a tree joining the 5 zones, so connecting all zones needs a spanning tree of 4 bridges (one fewer than the number of zones). The set {Q, R, T, V} is a valid spanning selection linking Z1 through Z5 with the minimum 4 bridges, matching the key.

q: The value of x such that x > 1, satisfying the equation ∫[1 to x] t ln t dt = 1/4 is
explanation: ∫ t ln t dt = (t²/2)ln t − t²/4. Evaluating from 1 to x gives (x²/2)ln x − x²/4 + 1/4 = 1/4, so (x²/2)ln x = x²/4, i.e. ln x = 1/2 for x > 1, giving x = √e.

Consider the following logic circuit diagram.

Which is/are the CORRECT option(s) for the output function F?
explanation: F is the OR of a NAND(X,Y) = ¬X+¬Y, a NOT(X) = ¬X, and an AND(X, NOT(Y)) = X¬Y, i.e. F = ¬X+¬Y+X¬Y. Since X¬Y is absorbed by ¬Y, this reduces to ¬X+¬Y = ¬(XY), so options (A), (B) and (C) are all algebraically equal to F, while (D) X+¬Y is not.

q:
Given the following Karnaugh Map for a Boolean function F(w, x, y, z):

Which one or more of the following Boolean expression(s) represent(s) F?
explanation: Reading the map, F = 1 exactly when x=0,z=0 or x=1,z=1, i.e. F = ¬x¬z + xz, which is option (D). Option (A)'s first four minterms are ¬x¬z with w and y ranging over all four combinations, which sums to exactly ¬x¬z, so (A) also equals ¬x¬z + xz = F. Options (B) and (C) omit some of those w,y combinations and so do not cover all of ¬x¬z.

q: Which of the following Boolean algebraic equation(s) is/are CORRECT?
explanation: (B) is the consensus theorem: BC is the consensus term of AB and ¬AC and is redundant, so AB + ¬AC + BC = AB + ¬AC. (C) expands to AĀ + AB + C̄A(sic) ... expanding (A+C)(¬A+B) = AB + ¬AC + BC, and BC is again the consensus term of AB and ¬AC, so it equals AB + ¬AC as claimed. (D) can likewise be verified to reduce to ¬AD + ¬C¬D by consensus/absorption. (A) does not simplify to the right-hand side, so it is excluded.

q:
Consider the following algorithm someAlgo that takes an undirected graph G as input.

someAlgo(G)
1. Let v be any vertex in G. Run BFS on G starting at v. Let u be a vertex in G at maximum distance from v as given by the BFS.
2. Run BFS on G again with u as the starting vertex. Let z be the vertex at maximum distance from u as given by the BFS.
3. Output the distance between u and z in G.

The output of someAlgo(T) for the tree shown in the given figure is ___________. (Answer in integer)
explanation: This double-BFS procedure is the standard algorithm for computing a tree's diameter. In the given tree, the two ends of a longest path (e.g. the leaf above the upper hub and the rightmost leaf on the lower-right chain) are 6 edges apart, so someAlgo(T) outputs 6.
